content_warnings.evidence: Gang, scam and syringe worries are comic hypotheticals; nothing sensitive happens.

difficulty.evidence: Many characters, including the mother's Yiddish-peppered voice.

performance_demands.evidence: The mother "peppers her words with Jewish phrases" and many callers are voiced.

audience_level.evidence: Little mature content.

themes.evidence: "I love my mother, but . . ."

subject_matter.value: Amy plays her mother's anxious answering-machine messages about weather, scams and safety and imagines the absurd results.
subject_matter.evidence: "So why does my mother always feel compelled to call me".

literary_form.evidence: A play with speaker labels and stage directions in a prison cell.

tone.evidence: A tender friendship ends in a joint suicide.

content_warnings.evidence: A shopkeeper "Shot Marcel in the neck", Dee's father "threw her down the stairs", Dee "stuck a bread knife in his side", white people "stick out a leg and trip me", and Jamie "pushes the knife into her own stomach" after Dee says "Do me first".

difficulty.evidence: Each actor plays a character at two ages with a very wide emotional range.

performance_demands.evidence: Young and adult versions of each woman plus mimed dusting and the stabbing.

audience_level.evidence: A suicide pact, domestic abuse and racist violence.

themes.evidence: "It's only when you walk with me you in trouble."

subject_matter.value: A Black and a white teenage inmate befriend each other in a 1950s prison, and years later, unable to survive together outside, they end their lives.
subject_matter.evidence: "We were happy when we were inside."

literary_form.evidence: A sketch from a play with speaker labels ANNETTE and GINA.

tone.evidence: The girls draw absurd lessons from West Side Story.

content_warnings.evidence: Killings are only recapped from a movie or posed as silly hypotheticals, so nothing sensitive happens in the scene.

difficulty.evidence: Two characters sustained in strong accents.

performance_demands.evidence: The note calls for "Strong Italian accents" and quick back-and-forth.

audience_level.evidence: References to sex and murder in the movie, played comically.

themes.evidence: "You are losing yourself in him, Annette."

subject_matter.value: Two Italian-American teen girls tearfully discuss West Side Story, loyalty and Annette's cheating boyfriend.

literary_form.evidence: A memoir by a 911 operator, split between narrators and callers.

tone.evidence: "Interesting? Yeah, but not amusing."

content_warnings.evidence: A girl reports her mother "shot herself. Oh my God.", a caller says he "slammed me up against the wall", a boy "was molested by a guy", and a teen's mother is "smoking crack".

difficulty.evidence: Sixteen roles from operators to panicked callers.

performance_demands.evidence: Directions such as "female screaming hysterically" and "calm and blasé".

themes.evidence: "Someone could die in my ear today"

subject_matter.value: Two 911 operators recount calls about a mother's suicide, domestic violence, drug use and child abuse, and how the work affects them.

literary_form.evidence: A ten-minute play with speaker labels GAIL and LYNETTE and stage directions.

tone.evidence: Lynette's comic proposition reverses into Gail's confession "Because I'm in love with you."

difficulty.evidence: Two characters with shifts from banter to confession.
